comment:
<comment datatype="string">ArnA is a bifunctional enzyme that acts within a pathway that modifies lipid A phosphates with 4-amino-4-deoxy-L-arabinose (L-Ara4N), which causes increased resistance to polymyxin [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/11706007">Breazeale02</a>]. 
<p>
ArnA exhibits UDP-glucuronic acid (UDP-GlcA) C-4"-dehydrogenase and UDP-4-amino-4-deoxy-L-arabinose (UDP-L-Ara4N) formyltransferase activities <i>in vitro</i> [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/11706007">Breazeale02</a>].  The two activities are separable, and both are required for polymyxin resistance [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/15695810">Breazeale05</a>].  
<p>
The N-terminal domain is similar to methionyl-tRNA<sup>fMet</sup> formyltransferase and catalyzes the <i>N</i><sup>10</sup>-formyltetrahydrofolate-dependent formylation of the 4'' amine of UDP-L-Ara4N [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/15695810">Breazeale05</a>].  Crystal structures of this domain have been solved at 1.7, 1.2 and 2.5 &Aring; resolution [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/15807526">GatzevaTopalova05a</a>, <a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/15809294">Williams05</a>, <a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/27171345">Genthe16</a>].  The <i>N</i><sup>10</sup>-formyltetrahydrofolate binding site has been identified and a reaction mechanism has been proposed; point mutations in the proposed catalytic residues abolish activity [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/15807526">GatzevaTopalova05a</a>, <a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/15809294">Williams05</a>].  The structure of the N-terminal domain in complex with both the UDP-sugar substrate and <i>N</i><sup>5</sup>-formyltetrahydrofolate has provided additional insight into the substrate binding site [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/27171345">Genthe16</a>].
<p>
The C-terminal domain contains the NAD<sup>+</sup>-dependent dehydrogenase/decarboxylase activity which catalyzes the oxidative decarboxylation of UDP-GlcA.  Crystal structures of this domain have been solved at 2.4 and 2.3 &Aring; resolution [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/15491143">GatzevaTopalova04</a>, <a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/15809294">Williams05</a>], and active site residues have been identified [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/15809294">Williams05</a>, <a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/15939024">GatzevaTopalova05</a>].  The C-terminal domain is also able to inefficiently catalyze the reduction of UDP-&alpha;-D-4-ketoxylose to UDP-&alpha;-D-xylose in an overall reaction similar to the human UDP-&alpha;-D-xylose synthase.  Local unfolding of the active site is proposed to direct formation of the preferred product [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/23072385">Polizzi12</a>]. 
<p>
Crystal structures of the full-length protein in the apo- and substrate-bound forms have been solved [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/15939024">GatzevaTopalova05</a>, <a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/25760615">Fischer15</a>].  The enzyme forms a homohexamer in a dimer-of-trimers configuration.  The dehydrogenase domain undergoes a large conformational change upon binding of the substrate UDP-GlcA; a catalytic mechanism was proposed [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/15939024">GatzevaTopalova05</a>].  A central pocket present in the unliganded structure is proposed to bind a small-molecule effector [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/25760615">Fischer15</a>].
<p>
ArnA was also identified as a protein that copurifies with the SsrA-SmpB complex [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/11248028">Karzai01</a>] and is often a contaminant during purification of recombinant His-tagged proteins [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/16814929">BolanosGarcia06</a>].
<p>
SAF: "<b>S</b>srA-<b>a</b>ssociated <b>f</b>actor" [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/11248028">Karzai01</a>]
<p>
ArnA: "L-<b>Ar</b>a4<b>N</b> (4-amino-4-deoxy-L-arabinose) biosynthesis" [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/11706007">Breazeale02</a>]
<p>
PmrI: "<b>p</b>oly<b>m</b>yxin <b>r</b>esistance"
<p>
Review: [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/17362200">Raetz07</a>]</comment>

<comment datatype="string"><a href="/gene?orgid=META&id=G7170">ArnT</a> is a transferase that catalyzes the addition of L-Ara4N residues from <a href="/compound?orgid=META&id=CPD0-1189">4-amino-4-deoxy-&alpha;-L-arabinopyranosyl <i>ditrans,octacis</i>-undecaprenyl phosphate</a> to lipid A. This modification confers on the organism resistance to the antibiotic polymyxin [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/11535604">Trent01a</a>, <a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/11535605">Trent01</a>].</comment>

<comment datatype="string">ArnF is an integral membrane component of the ArnE/ArnF undecaprenyl-phosphate-&alpha;-L-Ara4N
flippase.</comment>

<comment datatype="string">ArnC is an undecaprenyl transferase that acts in a pathway which modifies lipid A phosphates with 4-amino-4-deoxy-L-arabinose (L-Ara4N), causing increased resistance to polymyxin [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/11706007">Breazeale02</a>].  ArnC is an inner membrane protein with two predicted transmembrane domains; the C terminus is located in the cytoplasm [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/15919996">Daley05</a>].
<p>
ArnC selectively converts uridine 5'-diphospho-&beta;-(4-deoxy-4-formamido-L-arabinose) (UDP-L-Ara4FN), but not uridine 5'-diphospho-&beta;-(4-amino-4-deoxy-L-arabinose) (UDP-L-Ara4N), to lipid product [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/15695810">Breazeale05</a>].
<p>
ArnC: "L-<b>Ar</b>a4<b>N</b> (4-amino-4-deoxy-L-arabinose) biosynthesis" [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/11706007">Breazeale02</a>]
<p>

comment:
<comment datatype="string"><a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?object=Polymyxins" title="Polymyxins are antibiotics with a general structure consisting of a cyclic peptide with a long hydrophobic tail. They disrupt the structure of the bacterial cell membrane by interacting with its phospholipids. &#10;&#10;Polymyxins are produced by the Gram-positive bacterium <a href=''/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=ORGANISM&object=TAX-1406''><i>Paenibacillus polymyxa</i></a> and are selectively toxic for Gram-negative bacteria due to their specificity for the lipopolysaccharide molecules that exist within many Gram-negative outer membranes.">Polymyxins</a> are antibiotics with a general structure consisting of a cyclic peptide with a long hydrophobic tail. 
They are produced by the Gram-positive bacterium <a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=ORGANISM&object=TAX-1406"><i>Paenibacillus polymyxa</i></a> and are selectively toxic for Gram-negative bacteria due to their specificity for the lipopolysaccharide molecules that exist within many Gram-negative outer membranes. Polymyxins disrupt the structure of the bacterial cell membrane by interacting with its phospholipids, and specifically with lipid A. Lipid A is negatively charged due to two phosphate groups, and the cationic polymyxin readily binds to it and induces cell death by permeabilizing the bacterial membrane.
<p>
Some Gram-negative bacteria, specifically Salmonella typhimurium and <a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=ORGANISM&object=TAX-562"><i>Escherichia coli</i></a>, can become resistant to polymyxin by the modification of  their lipid A structure via the attachment of 4-amino-4-deoxy-L-arabinopyranose (L-Ara4N) groups to one or more phosphate groups [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/17686460">Fu07</a>, <a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/18467098">Gunn08</a>, <a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/19076233">Barchiesi09</a>, <a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/19767429">Pilonieta09</a>, <a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/21114395">Lim10</a>]. This addition causes an absolute increase in lipid A charge, thus lowering the affinity of positively charged polymyxins [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/18187325">Kline08</a>].
<p>
The modification of lipid A with 4-amino-4-deoxy-L-arabinopyranose (L-Ara4N) was first found in mutants of <a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=ORGANISM&object=TAX-562"><i>Escherichia coli</i></a> that are resistant to polymyxin [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/7565089">Nummila95</a>, <a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/11535605">Trent01</a>]. However, the pathway for the synthesis of L-Ara4N and its transport and attachment to lipid A has been studied mostly in Salmonella.
<p>
The pathway is well understood up to the formation of <a href="/compound?orgid=META&id=CPD0-888">4-deoxy-4-formamido-&alpha;-L-arabinopyranosyl <i>ditrans,octacis</i>-undecaprenyl phosphate</a> (UDP-Ara4FN). All steps up to this intermediate occur in the cytoplasm. UDP-Ara4FN is deformylated and transferred from the inner to the outer bacterial membrane by mechanisms that are not fully understood, although ArnE(PmrM) and ArnF(PmrL) may have a role in the transportation of UDP-Ara4FN across the bacterial inner membrane [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/17928292">Yan07</a>]. Once in the periplasm, LAra4N is transferred to lipid A by ArnT(PmrK) [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/15939024">GatzevaTopalova05</a>, <a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/12045108">Raetz02</a>, <a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/16226890">Bretscher06</a>] .
<p>
The pathway is regulated by the <a href="http://biocyc.org/ECOLI/new-image?object=PWY0-1482">BasSR Two-Component Signal Transduction System</a> (pmrA/pmrB). <a href="http://biocyc.org/ECOLI/new-image?object=EG11615">basR</a> is a response regulator that in its phosphorylated form can activate the genes that encode the proteins described in this pathway. Activation occurs either directly by Fe3+ ions [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/11051552">Wosten00</a>], or by a second two component system, the <a href="http://biocyc.org/ECOLI/new-image?object=PWY0-1458">PhoQP Two-Component Signal Transduction System, magnesium-dependent</a>, which is activated by low Mg2+ concentration [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/9371451">Groisman97</a>]. 
The two systems are linked in Salmonella by the polymyxin resistance protein, <a href="http://biocyc.org/ECOLI/new-image?object=G7172-MONOMER">PmrD</a>. The PhoP-activated PmrD protects the phosphorylated response regulator PmrA from dephosphorylation, and promotes the transcription of PmrA-activated genes responsible for polymyxin resistance [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/10775270">Kox00</a>]. In E. coli PmrD does not protect the phosphorylated <a href="http://biocyc.org/ECOLI/new-image?object=EG11615">basR</a>. This may be the reason why E. coli fails to activate the pathway under low Mg2+ concentrations [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/10373459">Zhou99a</a>].</comment>

comment:
<comment datatype="string">ArnT is a transferase that catalyzes the addition of L-Ara4N residues from <a href="/compound?orgid=META&id=CPD0-1189">4-amino-4-deoxy-&alpha;-L-arabinopyranosyl <i>ditrans,octacis</i>-undecaprenyl phosphate</a> to lipid A. This modification confers on the organism resistance to the antibiotic polymyxin [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/11535604">Trent01a</a>, <a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/11535605">Trent01</a>]. It should be noted that K-12 derived strains express ArnT, but do not synthesize  <a href="/compound?orgid=META&id=CPD0-1189">4-amino-4-deoxy-&alpha;-L-arabinopyranosyl <i>ditrans,octacis</i>-undecaprenyl phosphate</a> under normal conditions, and thus are sensitive to polymyxin.
<p>
The enzyme from E. coli has not been studied much, but the <i>Salmonella typhimurium</i> enzyme has been purified and characterized [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/11535604">Trent01a</a>, <a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/16226890">Bretscher06</a>].
<p>
It has been suggested, although not proven, that the enzyme is involved not only in the attachment of L-Ara4N to lipid A but also in the transport of L-Ara4N from the cytoplasm, where it is synthesized, to the periplasmic side of the inner membrane, where the attachment takes place.
<p>
Deletion of <I>arnT</I> results in defective attachment of L-Ara4N to the lipid A core, but does not affect the transport of undecaprenyl phosphate-&alpha;-L-Ara4N across the inner membrane [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/17928292">Yan07</a>].
<p>
A <I>lpxM</I> mutant lacking the secondary linked myristoyl group of lipid A is unable to attach L-Ara4N to lipid A [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/15951433">Tran05</a>].
<p>
Expression of the <I>arnBCADTEF</I> operon increased during growth with
elevated FeSO<sub>4</sub>, FeCl<sub>3</sub>, or ZnSO<sub>4</sub> and was
dependent upon the BasSR two-component signal transduction system
[<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/15322361">Hagiwara04</a>, <a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/15659689">Lee05d</a>]. The <i>arnT</i> transcript levels were increased under growth conditions with low Mg<sup>2+</sup> concentrations, but these expression levels decreased significantly in the <i>pmrD</i> mutant strain compared with the wild-type strain [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/25605366">Rubin15</a>].</comment>

comment:
<comment datatype="string">ArnB is a UDP-L-Ara4O C-4" transaminase [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/12704196">Breazeale03</a>] that acts in a pathway which modifies lipid A phosphates with 4-amino-4-deoxy-L-arabinose (L-Ara4N), causing increased resistance to polymyxin [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/11706007">Breazeale02</a>]. 
<p>
Structural and biochemical characterization of <i>Salmonella typhimurium</i> ArnB has been performed; crystal structures of the enzyme are presented and discussed with respect to catalysis [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/12429098">Noland02</a>].
<p>
Expression of <i>arnB</i> is induced by the presence of FeSO<sub>4</sub> (which primarily yields oxidized ferric iron in solution); the effect is dependent on the presence of the BasS-BasR two-component system [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/15322361">Hagiwara04</a>, <a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/16428424">Froelich06</a>].
<p>
ArnB: "L-<b>Ar</b>a4<b>N</b> (4-amino-4-deoxy-L-arabinose) biosynthesis" [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/11706007">Breazeale02</a>]
<p>
PmrH: "<b>p</b>oly<b>m</b>yxin <b>r</b>esistance" 
<p>
Review: [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/17362200">Raetz07</a>]</comment>

comment:
<comment datatype="string">The ArnE/ArnF undecaprenyl-phosphate-&alpha;-L-Ara4N flippase is responsible
for transporting undecaprenyl-phosphate-&alpha;-L-Ara4N from the cytoplasmic
face of the inner membrane to the periplasmic face of the inner membrane.
<p>
ArnE and ArnF are both predicted to be integral membrane proteins with 4
transmembrane helices and belong to the drug/metabolite transporter (DMT)
superfamily [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/17928292">Yan07</a>].  ArnE and ArnF may act as a heterodimer
[<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/17928292">Yan07</a>].
<p>
Deletion of <I>arnE</I> or <I>arnF</I> results in restoration of polymyxin
sensitivity in a polymyxin-resitant <I>pmrA<sup>c</sup></I> strain and are
defective for transfer of undecaprenyl-phosphate-&alpha;-L-Ara4N from the
cytoplasmic face of the inner membrane to the periplasmic face and for attachment
of L-Ara4N to lipid A [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/17928292">Yan07</a>].  Both ArnE and ArnF are required for
polymyxin resistance as expression from a plasmid of one cannot replace a deletion
of the other [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/17928292">Yan07</a>].
<p>
Expression of the <I>arnBCADTEF</I> operon increased during growth with
elevated FeSO<sub>4</sub>, FeCl<sub>3</sub>, or ZnSO<sub>4</sub> and was
dependent upon the BasSR two-component signal transduction system
[<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/15322361">Hagiwara04</a>, <a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/15659689">Lee05d</a>].</comment>

FUNCTION assigns production of UDP-aminoarabinose, and CATALYTIC ACTIVITY cites the reversible RHEA:24710 equation (ECO:0000269; PMID12704196).
Purified E. coli ArnB reversibly transfers the glutamate amino group to the UDP-ketopentose; NMR confirms the product, and the equilibrium constant toward UDP-aminoarabinose is about 0.1.
The homodimer SUBUNIT annotation is transferred by similarity from Salmonella Q8ZNF3 (ECO:0000250).
The native ArnA complex catalyzes the enzyme reaction linked to RXN0-1862.
CATALYTIC ACTIVITY assigns formyl transfer from (6R)-10-formyltetrahydrofolate to UDP-aminoarabinose (RHEA:24706; ECO:0000269); physiological direction is 24707.
The isolated E. coli N-terminal domain retains transformylation activity; assays add N10-formyltetrahydrofolate to the UDP-aminoarabinose substrate.

evidence.source_assertion: CATALYTIC ACTIVITY assigns transfer of formamidoarabinose from UDP to undecaprenyl phosphate (RHEA:27722; ECO:0000269; PMID15695810).
Only the formylated sugar nucleotide is converted in vitro to an undecaprenyl-phosphate-linked form by ArnC.
The native comment distinguishes ArnC utilization of UDP-L-Ara4FN from failure to utilize unformylated UDP-L-Ara4N.
The cryo-EM study uses Salmonella Typhimurium ArnC and observes apo and UDP-bound tetramers; this is not direct evidence for E. coli quaternary structure.
Substrate synthesis uses purified Salmonella ArnC in a reaction mixture containing MnCl2.
FUNCTION still labels deformylation probable (ECO:0000305); CATALYTIC ACTIVITY assigns RHEA:27734 with HAMAP and older PMID15695810 annotations.
E. coli K-12 pmrAc strain MST100 lacking arnD accumulates the formylated C55P-Ara4FN intermediate, supporting the cellular ArnD role.

evidence.source_assertion: Purified Salmonella Typhimurium ArnD deformylates the C55 donor; EDTA inhibition and Mn2+/Co2+ restoration or stimulation establish metal dependence in those assays.
The native E. coli ArnT protein links its catalyzed enzyme reaction to RXN0-2001; its comment states that the Salmonella enzyme was studied more extensively.
FUNCTION assigns L-Ara4N transfer from the lipid-linked donor to lipid A (ECO:0000269; PMID11535604). Its catalytic text specifically describes the lipid-IVA alternative.
The study reports two L-Ara4N additions to lipid-A precursors containing a Kdo disaccharide, but only one addition to lipid IVA lacking Kdo; ArnT homologs were assigned in E. coli and Salmonella.
Deletion of arnT in the E. coli pmrAc background abolishes lipid-A modification without the decreased donor accessibility observed for arnE/arnF mutants.

evidence.source_assertion: The COFACTOR field identifies pyridoxal 5-prime-phosphate.
Purified E. coli ArnB contains pyridoxal phosphate detected spectrophotometrically; excess glutamate converts it to the pyridoxamine form.
FUNCTION assigns transfer of the aminoarabinose-phosphoundecaprenol donor from cytoplasmic to periplasmic side of the inner membrane (ECO:0000269; PMID17928292).
Deleting either arnE or arnF reduces donor accessibility to an impermeable probe and restores sensitivity in the pmrAc parent; heterodimer formation and energy coupling remain proposals.

native_dispositions.decision: All six native biochemical reactions retained via independent MetaCyc/Rhea identities; the missing deformylase controller is supplied by later species-scoped evidence, not guessed from adjacency.
All six reactions and four protein/one complex source objects inspected as the Pseudomonas counterpart; no E. coli phenotype, exact assembly or metal inference transferred to it.
Native reaction name/EC2.1.2.13 is inconsistent with its dehydrogenase chemistry; current Rhea24703 and ArnA annotations ground oxidative decarboxylation.
Native two-substrate/two-water versus one-product stoichiometry rejected; Rhea27735 supplies the balanced unit equation.
No native external xref and its C61H100NO8P formula is copied from the formamido precursor; independent primary donor NMR and current Rhea/ChEBI resolve CHEBI60463, C60H100NO7P, charge0.
Native diphosphate return rejected; current balanced Rhea35372 returns two undecaprenyl monophosphates CHEBI60392, not diphosphate.
Older source marks hypothetical. Later E. coli arnD-disruption genetics and separately scoped purified Salmonella ArnD support the exact transformation; no E. coli physiological metal asserted.
Native folate classes retain their scope in the ledger; current Rhea specifies charged monoglutamate folates. No exactMatch of a class to one member is asserted.
Source bis-substituted product is retained with current balanced two-donor net stoichiometry; no two-transfer elementary event or universal cellular double substitution is asserted.

Proposed ArnE/ArnF heterodimer and transport represented as two qualified functional enables roles. No experimentally fixed physical complex, leaflet-specific chemical ID or known energy coupling is invented.
Ugd and Kdo2-lipid A assembly are outside the six-reaction native list. Existing lipid-IVA record is an upstream distinct pathway.

Every left/right occurrence is retained in the raw BioPAX projection and matched to the current complete Rhea equation by exact reaction/source context; inconsistent native labels/formulas/protonation are not silently copied. Native reaction-to-Rhea bridges are explicit edge evidence.
